This document guides AI agents on go-mapi. Prerequisites: Read [README.md](README.md) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Stack: C++ (MinGW), Go, TypeScript + React. Build: `npm run build` (or individual `npm run build:interceptor|native-host|extension`). Test: `npm run test`.

Pipeline: Windows App → [C++ DLL] → JSON files → [Go Native Host] → [Browser Extension] → Gmail API.

Principles: Privacy-focused; data stays local and minimize cloud exposure. Local-first; external API calls only when necessary (Gmail API for sending). Cost-conscious; prefer solutions that don't require paid services. Pragmatic. Type-safe; use TypeScript strict mode. Keep related things together; avoid excessive file splitting. Minimize bloat; single file for related components when reasonable. Colocation preferred. Use React Bootstrap, Radix UI, or similar. Avoid utility-first CSS: No Tailwind. Prefer semantic, maintainable markup. The project should be ready for translations from the start. Use message catalogs or i18n libraries for user-facing strings. Technical documentation remains in English.

Interceptor (`src/interceptor/`): Capture MAPI calls and write JSON files to `%TEMP%\go-mapi\`. Zero external dependencies (no nlohmann/json - hand-rolled JSON). Target Simple MAPI spec only (not Extended MAPI/COM). Non-blocking - return immediately to caller. Thread-safe - multiple apps may call simultaneously. `main.cpp` DLL entry point/exports; `mapi_impl.cpp` MAPISendMail; `json_writer.cpp` serialization; `fs_utils.cpp` filesystem. Always test with debug build: `npm run build:interceptor:debug`. Test with multiple calling applications (Explorer, PDF viewers, etc.). Check for memory leaks and thread safety.

Native Host (`src/native-host/`): Bridge filesystem to browser extension via Chrome Native Messaging. Protocol (length-prefixed JSON):
{"type": "email", "id": "...", "data": {...}}
{"type": "removed", "id": "..."}
{"type": "ready", "version": "1.0.0"}
{"type": "process", "id": "..."}
{"type": "delete", "id": "..."}
`main.go` entry/message loop; `protocol.go` protocol; `watcher.go` fsnotify watcher. Run `gofmt` before committing. Test native messaging with the extension. Handle filesystem edge cases (deleted files, permission errors).

Extension (`src/extension/`): UI and Gmail API integration. React 18, React Bootstrap, Vite, TypeScript. `manifest.json` manifest v3; `src/background/service-worker.ts` native messaging + Gmail API; `src/popup/App.tsx` main UI; `src/types/messages.ts` interfaces. Use React Bootstrap components for UI. Keep service worker minimal - offload to popup when possible. TypeScript strict mode is required. Test in both Chrome and Edge.

JSON files: `%TEMP%\go-mapi\*.json`; fields include `"subject"`, `"body"`, `"bodyFormat": "plain|html"`, `"to": [{"name": "John", "address": "<REDACTED_EMAIL>"}]`, attachments (`"filename"`, `"path"`, `"size"`), and `"originApp": "explorer.exe"`. Full schema: [docs/json-schema.json](docs/json-schema.json).

Docs: README user-focused; CONTRIBUTING developer-focused; AGENTS AI-focused; ROADMAP strategic planning. Comment the "why", not the "what". Document non-obvious constraints. Keep comments concise. Use Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`.

Workflow: understand affected component; read relevant source; check/run tests; identify related files. Follow existing patterns; keep changes minimal and focused; add tests; update docs when behavior changes. Run full build: `npm run build`; run tests: `npm run test`; manually test user-facing changes; write clear commit messages.

Personas: C++ Specialist (`src/interceptor/`): minimal, non-blocking, avoid dependencies. Go Developer (`src/native-host/`): filesystem watching/native messaging. Frontend Developer (`src/extension/`): React UI/Gmail integration. DevOps/CI (`.github/workflows/`): Windows builds.

Schema change: update `docs/json-schema.json`, C++ `json_writer.cpp`, TypeScript types in `src/extension/src/types/`, and Go structs in `src/native-host/`.

Setting: add to Chrome storage API; create settings UI; read in service worker; persist with `chrome.storage.sync`.

Release check: build all components: `npm run build`; register DLL (admin): `npm run register:mapi`; load extension in Chrome/Edge developer mode; check `%TEMP%\go-mapi\` JSON files; check extension DevTools.

Decisions: MinGW (GCC), not MSVC, for simpler setup/no Visual Studio and Scoop compatibility. React Bootstrap for component-first semantic markup. JSON files in `%TEMP%` for simple, debuggable cross-process communication without Windows API complexity.
